raw_findings.message: Because `init` is callable by anyone, an attacker can initialize the auction first with their own seller address and chosen parameters, locking out the intended seller.
If `duration_` makes the timestamp exceed `uint64`, the unchecked cast truncates `endTime` while `endBlock` uses the full duration, leaving the auction's time and block deadlines inconsistent.
Dividing `highestBid` by `BPS` before multiplying rounds down the increment; for bids below 10,000 the required increment is always zero, so bids can avoid the configured minimum increase.
The bid check permits bids during the 15-minute grace period even when both conditions in `hasEnded` are true, allowing bids after cancellation, finalization, or the bonus draw is already enabled.
A highest bidder contract that rejects ETH refunds makes this call revert, preventing every later bidder from outbidding it.
After refunding an outbid bidder, the contract leaves their `bidOf` entry intact, so they can cancel it and claim a second refund from funds backing other liabilities.
Every qualifying bid adds another entry even for an address already recorded, so a bidder can repeatedly bid to increase their chance of winning the bonus.
The recipient can re-enter `withdraw` before `pendingReturns` is cleared and withdraw the same balance repeatedly while the contract has enough funds.
There is no finalized flag, so anyone can call `finalize` repeatedly and transfer the same `highestBid` again, draining bonus funds or other users' deposits.
The bonus winner is chosen from timestamp and `prevrandao`, which a block producer can influence or selectively withhold to bias the draw.

raw_findings.message: Anyone can call `init` first and permanently choose the seller, reserve, duration, and increment, allowing an attacker to take over an auction before its intended setup.

Casting the unchecked timestamp-plus-duration value to `uint64` truncates large durations, which can make the auction end time incorrect and keep the auction open until an impractically large block number.

Dividing `highestBid` before multiplying by the basis points loses precision and can make the required increment substantially smaller than the configured percentage, especially for small bids or large increment settings.
A highest bidder contract that rejects ETH refunds causes every later bid to revert, letting that bidder block the auction from receiving higher bids.
The outbid bidder's `bidOf` entry is not cleared after this refund, so that bidder can later cancel the already-refunded amount and withdraw it again from funds belonging to the auction.
The highest bidder can cancel and withdraw their bid while `highestBid` and `highestBidder` remain unchanged, allowing the same amount to be paid again on an outbid or finalization.
`pendingReturns` is cleared only after the external call, so a recipient that reenters `withdraw` can withdraw the same balance repeatedly while the contract has sufficient funds.
`finalize` never marks the auction as finalized or clears the winning amount, so it can be called repeatedly to pay the same bid from bonus funds or other users' deposits.
The bonus winner is selected from block timestamp and `prevrandao`, which block producers can influence and callers can choose when to sample, allowing the draw outcome to be manipulated.

raw_findings.message: Anyone can initialize the auction and choose the seller and parameters, so an attacker who calls `init` first can direct the proceeds to themselves.
The unchecked cast truncates large durations to `uint64`, which can make `endTime` wrap into the past while `endBlock` remains far in the future and leave the auction open for an extremely long time.
Dividing `highestBid` before multiplying makes the increment too small and zero for bids below 10,000, allowing bids that do not meet the configured percentage increase.
When an outbid bidder is refunded, their `bidOf` entry is not cleared, so they can later cancel and withdraw that already-refunded amount from funds backing other claims.
The current highest bidder can cancel and withdraw their bid while `highestBid` and `highestBidder` remain unchanged, leaving the auction able to pay the seller for a bid that was already returned.
The external call occurs before `pendingReturns` is cleared, so a recipient can reenter `withdraw` and withdraw repeatedly against funds backing other bidders or the bonus pool.
`hasEnded` ignores the 15-minute grace period accepted by `bid`, so bids can still be placed after the auction is considered ended and even after it is finalized.
`finalize` never records that it has paid out or clears the winning bid, so anyone can call it repeatedly and drain funds reserved for pending returns or the bonus pool.
The bonus winner is selected using block timestamp and `prevrandao`, which block producers can influence and callers can exploit to bias the prize draw.
